provenance.l: Apollo 11 Mission Report MSC-00171 (Nov 1969): Table 7-VII, entry interface 195:03:05.7 at 400,000 ft, 36,194.4 ft/s (11,032 m/s), -6.48 deg, peak 6.56 g; Table A-I, command module weight at entry 12,095.5 lb (5,486 kg)

Apollo 11 Entry Postflight Analysis (MSC Mission Planning and Analysis Division, Feb 1970): hypersonic CM L/D 0.282 (reconstructed); relative range 1,497 n.mi (2,772 km) from entry to the target; lift-up held until the drag passed 1.426 g at 52 s, bank -180 deg after the first pulse; first maximum load factor 6.73 g at 82 s, minimum 0.48 g, second maximum 6.00 g. Model limit: with these inputs the model peaks at 8.0 g at 68 s (first pulse), 0.42 g, 5.4 g; drogues 578 s (541 s flown), splashdown 935 s (929 s flown)

Apollo 11 Mission Report: drogues deployed at 195:12:06.9 (no altitude published); splashdown 195:18:35 GET (16:50:35 GMT 24 July 1969) at 13.30 N, 169.15 W, USS Hornet (Table 3-I, section 7.5; NASA SP-4029)
Apollo Flight Journal, Apollo 11 day 9: entry and splashdown (mains at about 3 km, barometric switch)
Apollo CM entry aero (L/D 0.3), drogue and main areas: the Apollo 8 profile (MSC-PA-R-69-1), same Block II command module
